text:
jamie: Need a quick product decision for Performance Lane pilot. Two options: strict short-term SLA lanes vs. prepaid Burst Packs. Pilot needs one path.

sara: Field: customers want predictable behavior during peaks. Prefer buy-now burst that just works.

ivan: Finance prefers prepaid packs + overage pricing. Hard SLAs require higher price and capacity reservation.

micah: PMM: Positioning should be simple. "Burst Pack" works well. Need buyer kit + worked examples.

priya: Legal: we must label bursts as best-effort unless customer pays for reserved capacity. Add preemption clause.

legal-bot: Suggested snippet: "Burst Credits increase scheduling priority but do not create a performance guarantee. Redwood may throttle or revoke bursts to protect platform stability."

pricing-bot: Recommend surge multiplier = 3x for on-demand top-ups. Logged ticket PR-820.

ivan: also propose billing unit = concurrency-minute (1 credit = 1 concurrent request for 60s). Engineering says easier to enforce.

micah: Sales hates "concurrency-minute" wording. Need UI that shows cost per API-call equivalent.

jamie: Decision for pilot (proposal): baseline reserved per-route, plus Burst Packs sold in packs (concurrency-minutes). Best-effort bursts, 3x surge for top-ups. Pilot gated on perf bench + two pilot customers.

sara: I'll recruit pilots and draft buyer kit.

priya: I'll drop contract language and ensure SOW has fallback model variant clause.

ivan: I'll produce simple example pricing calc.

jamie: Sync ops tomorrow 10am PT to validate throttling sim. Thanks :thumbsup:
